competency_fulfillment.rationale: The competency requires composing AND decomposing figures built from six shape types (squares, rectangles, triangles, circles, half circles, quarter circles) via cut-outs and square grids, but the only visible pattern -- counting shapes in a fixed rectangle-plus-triangle figure -- exercises just the decompose-by-counting slice and never shows circles, half/quarter-circles, cut-outs, or square-grid framing.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: All 5 sampled seeds (42 through 46) returned the exact byte-identical question 'A figure is made of a rectangle with a triangle on top. How many shapes make up this figure?' with answer 2 every time, despite a registered shapes_2d space of 3 axes and 24 combos -- a genuine low-diversity signal, not just a thin illustrative subset.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: The two sentences making up the prompt run about 12 and 7 words respectively, comfortably inside the Grade 2 Quarter 1 18-word cap, so reading load itself is appropriate even though sample variety is the problem here, not sentence length.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: A 24-combo registry ought to rotate through different shape pairings (squares with triangles, circles with rectangles, and so on) and both compose and decompose directions, but since every one of 5 seeds returned the identical rectangle-triangle pairing, that breadth cannot be confirmed from the evidence given.

competency_alignment.rationale: The single visible question type addresses only the 'decompose by counting parts' slice of a competency that explicitly names six shape types and two operations (compose and decompose) plus two tools (cut-outs, square grids), so alignment is partial rather than the full scope of this node's wording.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Content here is discrete shape-counting (2 shapes making up a figure), not a continuous numeric range, so scale/magnitude is not the concern for this node -- the concern lies in sample diversity instead.
